Subject: Order Form v3 — OSS/model liability carve-outs

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our latest Order Form with a small set of redlines from procurement and legal. Two items they are pushing hard on that I'd like to surface up-front:

1) Open-source/model pass-through liability — they want explicit pass-through liability for third-party OSS model licensors up to the same cap as the vendor (no additional stacking).
2) Consequential damages carve-outs — they are asking for the standard mutual exclusion to be narrowed so that certain compliance failures (e.g., data exfiltration caused by model behavior) remain excluded for Redwood.

We know Redwood prefers a single overall cap tied to fees; procurement is proposing a carve-out for IP/OSS indemnity and wants to see language that limits our exposure to licensors and redistributors. Can you confirm who on your side should weigh in (legal/engineering) and a realistic timeline to get a counter?

Attachment: OpenMetric_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx

Best,
Sophie Turner

Karthik / Ben / Naomi — looping you in. OpenMetric wants pass-through for OSS/model licensors and a narrower consequential exclusion. Quick thoughts:

- Ben: legal — we should avoid creating an open-ended pass-through that increases our net cap. Proposal: allow pass-through only to the extent that (a) the third party contract expressly requires indemnity and (b) the total pass-through amount cannot exceed the Order Form cap. Also carve the pass-through into a specific OSS/model indemnity bucket with a higher sub-cap?
- Naomi: sales/procure — are you ok pushing back on a separate OSS carve-out? If they insist, we may trade a modest sub-cap increase for better termination/fix rights and stronger notice/defense control.
- Karthik: CS/solutions — any engineering exposure we should flag (e.g., model licensing that requires source-availability obligations)?

I will draft a short counter and propose a call if they want to escalate.

— Lauren

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order Form v3 — OSS/model liability carve-outs

Lauren — quick legal note and suggested redline language below.

Legal note: we cannot accept unlimited pass-throughs that sit outside the mutual cap. Two guardrails that work in practice:
(1) Pass-through permitted only where the third party agreement requires indemnity/defense of the customer and we have no practical ability to obtain indemnity from that third party.
(2) Aggregate exposure for pass-through claims is subject to the Order Form aggregate liability cap. No layering beyond that.

Suggested redline (short):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer may seek recovery from Vendor for amounts Vendor is required to pay to third-party licensors of open-source software or model components ("OSS Pass-Through Claims") provided that (i) such amounts result from a final adjudication or settlement binding on Vendor, (ii) Vendor had contractual responsibility to pay such amounts under a binding agreement with such third party, and (iii) the aggregate of all OSS Pass-Through Claims shall be included within and not in addition to the Vendor liability cap set forth in this Order Form."

Consequential damages carve-out: we push for mutual broad exclusion but include an explicit exception for breaches of confidentiality and gross negligence. If OpenMetric insists on narrowing further for regulatory claims, we can add a short carve-out limited to proven direct regulatory fines but only up to the cap.

I'll prepare a clean counter-marked Order Form with these provisions and a one-page summary for their procurement team.

— Ben
Legal Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Turner <contracts@openmetric.com>

Subject: Re: Order Form v3 — OSS/model liability carve-outs

Lauren / Ben — thanks for the fast turnaround and the suggested language. Procurement is comfortable with the inclusion of OSS Pass-Through Claims so long as it is expressly permitted in the Order Form and we have parity with other vendors. A couple of follow-ups from legal: 

- Could Redwood confirm that the "final adjudication or settlement" standard will not unduly delay commercial remedies (OpenMetric needs a path to early resolution where appropriate).
- For the consequential damages carve-out, we prefer an explicit carve-out for IP infringement and regulatorily-triggered liabilities tied to model outputs. If Redwood will accept those, can we get a clearer cap number (OpenMetric's procurement is aiming for parity with their existing vendor cap of USD 2,500,000 for OSS-related claims).

If you're comfortable, let's schedule a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow to finalize. We can exchange a DocuSign link afterward for the revised Order Form.

Attachment: redlines_summary.pdf

Best,
Sophie
